key_insight: TEPID-ADAPT-VQE can variationally target multiple low-lying excited states at once by diagonalizing a truncated thermal density matrix, while keeping the ansatz compact through adaptive circuit growth.
engineering_relevance: This provides a near-term quantum chemistry workflow for computing excited-state energies and potential energy surfaces with fewer problem-specific tuning choices than comparable adaptive methods.
method: Build a truncated low-temperature Gibbs state to focus on the excited-state manifold of interest.
Use ADAPT-style operator selection to construct compact, system-tailored circuits.
Compare against a modified MORE-ADAPT-VQE baseline across several molecules and bond lengths.
evidence_signal: Across H2, LiH, and linear H4, the abstract reports chemical-accuracy agreement for excited-state spectra and potential energy curves in both weakly and strongly correlated regimes.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on choosing an appropriate temperature hyperparameter, since it sets the energy window of targeted excited states.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of molecular excited-state manifolds and energies using the TEPID-ADAPT-VQE algorithm
